title: Daily Market Digest: July 30, 2026
subtitle: Market rallies on tech strength despite mixed economic data.

items.headline: Tech Leads Market Rebound as Microsoft Surges; Fed Holds Rates Steady
items.summary: U.S. equities rallied on Thursday, primarily driven by a surge in technology stocks following robust earnings from Microsoft. The broader market sentiment showed resilience, recovering from Wednesday's selloff, despite the Federal Reserve's decision to maintain interest rates and mixed economic data releases. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East continued to be a backdrop, though investors largely focused on corporate earnings and monetary policy signals. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Microsoft (MSFT) Leads Tech Surge
items.summary: Shares of Microsoft ($MSFT) surged 15.2% today, lifting the broader technology sector. The strong performance followed the software giant's robust fiscal fourth-quarter earnings, which beat Wall Street expectations, fueled by accelerating AI and cloud demand. Its Azure cloud business notably surpassed $100 billion in annual revenue for the first time.

items.headline: MarketAxess (MKTX) Soars on Acquisition News
items.summary: MarketAxess Holdings ($MKTX) soared 30% after Intercontinental Exchange ($ICE) agreed to acquire the electronic trading platform. The move was further supported by MarketAxess's strong second-quarter results, which beat expectations.

items.headline: Lam Research (LRCX) Gains on Strong Guidance
items.summary: Lam Research ($LRCX) jumped 18.2% after reporting strong fiscal fourth-quarter earnings and robust forward revenue guidance. Continued demand tied to artificial intelligence also fueled the gains.

items.headline: Alnylam Pharma (ALNY) Tumbles on Missed Forecasts
items.summary: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals ($ALNY) tumbled 29.4% today after missing its second-quarter revenue forecasts and issuing a disappointing full-year guidance revision.

items.headline: Meta Platforms (META) Falls on Weak Guidance
items.summary: Meta Platforms ($META) shares fell 8.9% after the social media giant missed earnings forecasts and issued weaker-than-expected revenue guidance, raising investor concerns about the return on its AI investments.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady, Three Dissent
items.summary: The Federal Reserve concluded its policy meeting on Wednesday by holding its key interest rate steady in the range of 3.5%-3.75% for the fifth consecutive meeting. However, the decision was not unanimous, with three officials dissenting in favor of a quarter-point rate hike amidst persistent inflation concerns. J.P. Morgan now anticipates a rate hike in December, bringing forward its previous forecast.

items.headline: U.S. Economy Slows in Q2, Inflation Moderates Slightly
items.summary: The U.S. economy grew at an annualized rate of 1.5% in the second quarter, falling short of economists' expectations of 1.8%. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, fell 0.1% for the month, bringing the annual rate to 3.7%, matching expectations. Core PCE, excluding food and energy, rose 0.1% for the month and 3.3% year-over-year.

items.headline: Technology and AI Sectors Drive Gains
items.summary: The technology sector spearheaded today's market rally, largely buoyed by Microsoft's strong earnings report and continued optimism around artificial intelligence investments. Chip stocks like Micron ($MU) and SanDisk ($SNDK) also saw significant gains, with Micron jumping 14.75% and SanDisk rising 20.74%, as Microsoft's robust AI growth eased concerns about overall AI spending. The Nasdaq-100 Equal Weighted Index has notably outperformed its market-cap weighted counterpart in 2026, suggesting broader market participation beyond mega-cap tech stocks.

items.headline: Key Earnings Reports and Upcoming Releases
items.summary: Beyond Microsoft and Meta, several other companies reported earnings today. EMCOR Group ($EME) and Lam Research ($LRCX) posted strong results and raised guidance, contributing to their significant stock gains. Hershey ($HSY), American Electric Power ($AEP), Enterprise Products Partners ($EPD), and Valero Energy ($VLO) also reported their second-quarter results today. Investors are now keenly awaiting after-hours earnings reports from major players like Apple ($AAPL) and Amazon ($AMZN).
